partners.mechanism_chain: SLC25A20 (HGNC:10771) —DISRUPTS→ carnitine shuttle (GO:0015724); carnitine shuttle (GO:0015724) —DECREASES→ acylcarnitines (CHEBI:16777); acylcarnitines (CHEBI:16777) —LEADS_TO→ hypoketotic hypoglycemia (HP:0003110); CPT2 (HGNC:2595) —DISRUPTS→ fatty acid oxidation (METABOLIC:fatty acid oxidation); fatty acid oxidation (METABOLIC:fatty acid oxidation) —DECREASES→ acylcarnitines (CHEBI:16777); acylcarnitines (CHEBI:16777) —LEADS_TO→ lethargy (HP:0011425). partners.diseaseBName: lethal congenital glycogen storage disease of heart
partners.mechanism_chain: SLC25A20 (HGNC:10938) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0006635); SLC25A20 (HGNC:10938) —DECREASES→ Carnitine (CHEBI:17487); Mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0006635) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0006618); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0006618) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001637); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0006618) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac dysfunction (HP:0011674); PRKAG2 (HGNC:9575) —INCREASES→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0006618); Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001637) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac dysfunction (HP:0011674). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC25A20 impair carnitine transport into mitochondria, disrupting fatty acid beta-oxidation and subsequently reducing mitochondrial ATP synthesis. Gain-of-function mutations in PRKAG2, encoding a subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), lead to aberrant activation of AMPK, which paradoxically can disrupt mitochondrial ATP synthesis regulation and promote glycogen accumulation in the heart. Both pathways converge on impaired mitochondrial ATP synthesis and lead to cardiac dysfunction and cardiomyopathy.

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC25A20 (HGNC:10487) —DISRUPTS→ carnitine shuttle (REACT:R-HSA-74895); carnitine shuttle (REACT:R-HSA-74895) —DISRUPTS→ long-chain fatty acid oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-1435095); CPT1A (HGNC:2580) —DISRUPTS→ long-chain fatty acid oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-1435095); long-chain fatty acid oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-1435095) —LEADS_TO→ hypoglycemia (HP:0001250); long-chain fatty acid oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-1435095) —LEADS_TO→ hypoketotic hypoglycemia (HP:0003472); long-chain fatty acid oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-1435095) —LEADS_TO→ cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Variants in SLC25A20 impair the carnitine shuttle, which is essential for transporting long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondria for oxidation. Variants in CPT1A directly impair the first committed step of long-chain fatty acid oxidation within the mitochondria. Both defects lead to a deficiency in energy production from fatty acids, resulting in overlapping phenotypes like hypoglycemia and cardiomyopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in SLC25A20 in a patient diagnosed with carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A deficiency, or vice versa, without evidence of a shared underlying mechanism, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, demonstration that the specific variants do not lead to loss-of-function of the respective proteins would also be falsifying. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in SLC25A20 or CPT1A with a gnomAD allele frequency greater than 0.01% would suggest they are not solely responsible for rare disease phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on the long-chain fatty acid oxidation pathway for both carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase deficiency and carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A deficiency highlights potential therapeutic targets. Strategies aimed at supporting alternative energy substrates or improving mitochondrial function could be beneficial for patients with either condition.
